title: ABL kinase + imatinib
caption: The ABL kinase domain (the business end of BCR-ABL1) with imatinib (sticks) wedged in its pocket. Imatinib holds the kinase in an 'off' shape.

title: KRAS G12C + sotorasib
caption: Mutant KRAS G12C with sotorasib (AMG 510) bound in the 'switch-II' pocket next to the mutated cysteine, plus GDP. This pocket was the breakthrough that ended KRAS's 'undruggable' reputation.

title: Normal KRAS + GDP
caption: Normal KRAS holding GDP, its 'off' signal molecule. The protein surface is smooth with no obvious deep pocket, which is why drug makers struggled for decades.

title: p53 gripping DNA
caption: The DNA-binding part of p53 clamped onto DNA. Most cancer mutations in TP53 hit this region and stop it from gripping DNA.

title: CDK6 + palbociclib
caption: CDK6 with palbociclib in the pocket where ATP (the cell's fuel molecule) would normally sit.

title: DHFR + methotrexate
caption: Human DHFR with methotrexate, an old chemotherapy that looks like the enzyme's natural partner, folate.

title: MDM2 + nutlin-3a
caption: MDM2 with nutlin-3a sitting in the groove where p53 normally docks. Block the groove and p53 is set free.

title: PARP1 + olaparib
caption: The catalytic part of PARP1 with olaparib bound.

title: BCL-2 + navitoclax
caption: BCL-2 (a close cousin of BCL-XL) with navitoclax in the groove the protein uses to grab and silence 'death' proteins.

title: Thymidylate synthase + raltitrexed
caption: Thymidylate synthase, the target of 5-fluorouracil, shown here with dUMP and raltitrexed (a different drug that blocks the same enzyme).

title: Topoisomerase II + etoposide + DNA
caption: Topoisomerase IIβ (a close cousin of TOP2A) trapped on cut DNA by etoposide.

title: Topoisomerase I + camptothecin + DNA
caption: Topoisomerase I stuck on DNA by camptothecin, the natural compound topotecan was made from.

title: Proteasome + bortezomib
caption: The whole 20S proteasome, the cell's protein shredder, with bortezomib bound. It's big: give it a few seconds to load.
